screening_results.reason: This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 24–37; N=10 for fMRI) using socially relevant non-verbal vocalizations and animated faces, addressing social-related perception/understanding of others. Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, maps transformed to Talairach space, thresholded maps and ROI analyses) are presented as group activation maps (figures/tables), satisfying group whole-brain voxelwise reporting (not merely ROI-based). Healthy adult results are reported separately and clearly. Although slice coverage was focused on temporal cortex, the paper presents group voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy sample, meeting the review’s requirements.

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production tied to social communication and empathy (social-related processing). Sample: 19 healthy, right-handed native-English adults aged 18–58 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) thresholded and corrected (p<0.05 FDR, cluster k>5) and describes coordinates and supplementary materials; overlap/SVC and whole-brain contrasts are reported in text and figures. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI during social tasks in healthy adults (theory-of-mind and social attribution-of-attention) and meets I3 and I4. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy group. Task-related analyses were performed using localized ICA within a TPJ ROI (ROI-limited task decomposition) and task relevance was assessed via IC time-course regressions; whole-brain results are limited to seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E3.

The study uses task fMRI during a social-related face encoding/recognition paradigm (meets I3) and includes healthy adult participants (young subgroup aged 20–31; meets I4). However, the imaging analyses reported are region-of-interest (amygdala) extractions and parameter estimates; the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain results for the healthy group. Because no unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy group is provided, the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using an explicit social task (imitate/observe emotional faces) probing perception/understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group-level analyses (PLS and GLM) with voxelwise brain maps rendered in MNI space and thresholded voxel patterns reported, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Healthy participant results are reported for the group (neuroimaging data from 20 participants used for final analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level task activation data.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that involves perception and understanding of others’ emotions. The sample comprises healthy adults (final fMRI sample N=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects paired t-tests, TFCE FWE-corrected results) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI whole-brain task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, combined N=59) performing social-related semantic tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant words), satisfying the review’s social-processing target. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and peak coordinates presented, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control participants; ROI analyses are supplementary. Study 2 includes control participants reported separately from patient data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of interactive joint-action (leading vs following) that probes social cognitive processes (mentalizing, perception of others) during a social task. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean ages ~40) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, Following>Leading, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and whole-brain regression analyses; results are presented for the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social perception (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified for the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to be across all participants or focus on group contrasts (BPD vs controls) and ROI analyses for the amygdala are reported for controls. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a clear, group-level whole-brain healthy/control task map; that requirement is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts or pooled analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a socioemotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces) during functional MRI, addressing social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises 49 healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) with results reported for this healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (F > N, N > F) using whole-brain TFCE/FWE-corrected analyses, including coordinates, figures, and descriptions in the text (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) probing social exclusion/affiliation processes in healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates (including clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction) and provides coordinate tables and described contrasts for the healthy/control sample. All required inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in healthy adults are met, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (visual processing of dyadic interactions), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain preprocessing and GLM estimation to generate run-wise whole-brain beta maps and report group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests) and whole-brain searchlight analyses. Results include group-level voxelwise classification/searchlight findings and discussion of whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses/maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or resting-state-only) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social neuroeconomic task (prisoners' dilemma) probing social behaviour and cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; ages 18–50) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the control group (one-sample t-tests and per-group analyses with whole-brain results described and visualized; thresholding and cluster reporting are provided), satisfying the requirement for unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. Constructs assessed (trust/cooperation, mentalizing, face trustworthiness) fall within social-related processing. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (dynamic facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group (TD). The reported whole-brain analyses focus on between-group comparisons and found no significant additional activations; the main task results are given as ROI/MANCOVA analyses and DCM (effective connectivity). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study that examines perception of eye gaze (a social communication cue) and face identity in healthy adults (n=9, mean age 24), satisfying the social-related task and healthy adult sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (faces vs control; attention to identity vs gaze; averted vs direct gaze) identified with voxelwise thresholds (z>4) and cluster criteria, with coordinates reported using SPM/Talairach and figures/tables presenting activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy/sample outside age range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). While the study clearly used fMRI to examine responses to racial ingroup vs outgroup faces (meets I3), the available content does not report participant ages or confirm that the sample were healthy adults aged 18–65 (cannot confirm I4). Crucially, the abstract describes ROI analyses of amygdala voxels and does not provide clear evidence of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy group; I5 cannot be confirmed. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria (I4, I5) cannot be verified from the provided content, the study must be excluded pending a complete article. No formal exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the truncated content, so exclusion is due to unmet/uncertain inclusion criteria and incomplete full text.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: the study uses fMRI for social-related tasks (empathy and forgivability), so I3 is met. However, participant ages are not reported (only 'ten volunteers'), so I4 cannot be confirmed. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are implied by reported activated regions but not verifiably presented in the provided text, so I5 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available excerpt. Because core information required to confirm all inclusion criteria (notably I4 and I5) is missing, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (14 analyzed; ages 18–30) performing social judgments (trustworthiness of faces), directly addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). Group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPMs, contrasts, coordinates, and figures) including whole-brain results and small-volume corrections; coordinates and statistical maps are clearly described in the text and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (causal attribution/self-responsibility and self-serving bias) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 12 neurologically healthy adults (ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM99 fixed-effects, voxelwise corrections) with tables of peak coordinates and figures showing activations for contrasts of interest (internal vs external attributions; self-serving vs non-self-serving). All inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level results are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (learning moral status via cooperative/defective play) in healthy adults (scanned sample: 11 right-handed participants, age range 21–36), addressing social perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (contrasts and tables of coordinates, reported activations across whole-brain regions and predefined ROIs), satisfying whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=13, mean age 27.2) using a social-related task (passive viewing of video clips depicting social interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA) with conservative multiple-comparison correction (P ≤ 0.05 whole-brain corrected), and presents peaks/clusters in tables and figures comparing relational vs. alone and vs. rest. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants using a social task (mutual vs. averted gaze), meeting the review’s scope for social processing. The sample includes healthy young adults (fMRI N=8) meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports voxel-based, group-level whole-brain activation maps (t-statistic activation maps and visualization on a standard brain) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and not a non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adult participants (N=12, ages 21–28). The task is explicitly social and relevant to social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects contrasts, voxel-level thresholds reported) and describes results in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment), using a task tapping perception/understanding of self and others. Sample: 19 healthy adult participants (age range within 18–65) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (contrasts G−N, E−N, E−G, G−E) with statistical parametric maps, coordinate tables, thresholds, and figures. Results are presented as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, outside age range, non-empirical) are met.

Full text is not provided (PDF only/metadata and abstract only). Abstract indicates fMRI experiments addressing social understanding (satisfies I3). However participant details and age range are not reported in the available content so I4 cannot be confirmed. Methods and results are missing, so it is not possible to verify that a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported (I5 not confirmed). Per screening rules, all inclusion criteria must be verifiable; inability to confirm I4 and I5 requires exclusion. Recommend obtaining full article PDF to re-screen.

This fMRI study examines self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing perception/understanding of self), uses an event-related task with healthy adult participants (N=10, mean age 26.9), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, Z-stat maps thresholded, and Tables of MNI coordinates for contrasts). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text reports an empirical fMRI study probing social cognition (impression formation about people vs objects) in healthy adults. Sample: 14 healthy adults (ages 18.3–23.7) satisfying the adult age range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM99; voxel-based threshold P<0.001; clusters >10 voxels) with contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types) and coordinates/tables/figures provided. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-face recognition — perception/understanding of self) using task BOLD fMRI (event-related) in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed male undergraduates, mean age 19.36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (unknown vs scrambled, familiar vs unknown, self vs familiar) analyzed in SPM2 with thresholding and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-age-range samples, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.4, N=15) investigating processing of angry prosody (social communication/perception of others) with selective attention manipulations—clearly a social-related task. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM2 random-effects, whole-brain contrasts, coordinates and cluster-level correction reported). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion; healthy-group results are presented (not limited to an ROI or connectivity-only analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy) using a visual cartoon task—meets social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (13 right-handed males, ages 19–36) with psychiatric screening—meets sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (ToM − Physical1, Empathy − Physical2), conjunction and interaction analyses using random-effects SPM2, with coordinates/tables of activation foci—meets whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an fMRI study of social interaction using virtual characters (social communication), with event-related whole-brain analyses reported (SPM2, voxelwise maps, coordinates, tables, figures). Sample: 18 healthy adult males (mean age 25.9), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SOC>ARB, ARB>SOC, ME>OTHER, OTHER>ME, interactions) with stereotactic coordinates and figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly addressing perception/understanding of self (distinguishing own vs external movement), which falls under the social-related construct list. The sample includes healthy adults (ages 20–28; n=16 with one excluded for motion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps and their comparisons) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, coordinates, and figures/tables. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), conducted in healthy adults (N=11, ages 18–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts using random-effects analyses with tables of coordinates, cluster volumes, and t-values for multiple contrasts (faces associated with behaviors vs. novel faces; negative vs. positive; disgusting vs. aggressive). All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary only and does not include core full-text details (methods, participant demographics/ages, whole-brain statistical maps or tables). Based on available information: the study is an fMRI investigation of face perception (social-related processing) so I3 is met. However, I cannot verify sample age range and healthy-adult reporting (I4) nor confirm that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked map for the healthy group is reported (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone, but because essential information is missing, the study cannot be confirmed as eligible. Exclude pending access to the complete full text with participant details and whole-brain results.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI in a social interactive paradigm (competitive reaction-time/retaliation and observation of an opponent), addressing social processing; (I4) sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=16 males, mean age 28.6); (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects SPM2, voxelwise thresholding, FDR correction, tables of coordinates and activation maps) clearly from the healthy participant group; (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition: participants (healthy adult undergraduates, mean age ~19.5) viewed images of social groups and made affective/social judgments while BOLD data were recorded. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) task-evoked contrasts with Talairach coordinates and region activations (mPFC, insula, amygdala). It therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social conceptual processing (judgments of social concept meaning relatedness), uses a healthy adult sample (n=26; mean age 29.4 within 18–65), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (social vs. animal; conjunction analyses) with coordinates and figures. Results are reported for the healthy group and whole-brain findings are described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adults (N=29, ages 20–35 and 23–33), reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (FWE-corrected results and tables/figures) for explicit and implicit conditions. The healthy participant results are reported as a distinct group. The full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies the review’s requirements for inclusion.

The study is an fMRI investigation of self-referential processing and perspective taking (social cognition constructs), using a task where participants judge trait adjectives about self and close others — meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (adult sample), meeting I4. The abstract reports task-evoked activations in multiple MPFC regions (group-level activation contrasts), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise results, meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. However, the provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the full article (methods/results/discussion not fully present), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; this reduces certainty that full reporting (e.g., explicit whole-brain maps/coordinates) is present in the manuscript. Recommend retrieval of the complete article to confirm all details and extract coordinates if needed.

This is an fMRI study of communicative speech (a social-communication task) in healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–24). This is an empirical fMRI study (task-based) on social communication/intent understanding (communicative vs private intentions), using healthy adult participants (N=23, mean age ~24). This is an fMRI study of social communicative gesture processing and imitation in healthy adults. This paper reports an fMRI task investigating recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’ (social perception/understanding of others), using task-based whole-brain analyses. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating theory-of-mind/emotion/pain processing (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (N=46, ages 18–31). This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using a social-related task (perception of nonverbal dyadic interactions) in healthy adults (21 right-handed male participants, ages 23–33).
