This is an fMRI study of social self-processing (direct and reflected self-evaluations from peers) that clearly falls within social-related processing constructs (Perception/Understanding of Self and Others). The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31) reported separately alongside adolescents. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA) with corrected voxelwise and cluster thresholds and displays main effects and interaction maps (figures/tables). Separate age-group analyses are indicated (with supplementary materials referenced) and whole-brain ROI and voxelwise results are reported, satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task effects are available (including tables/figures/supplement). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect: observing emergencies with varying group sizes) meeting all inclusion criteria. I3: Task is social-related (perception/understanding of others) using movies of emergencies. I4: Sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–27 (group results reported). I5: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, parametric maps, cluster-corrected results; tables/figures of coordinates/clusters). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social cognitive processing (causal attribution/mentalizing), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI during social/mentalizing task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–41, N=20, results reported for this group), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected results; Table 1 and conjunction/contrast whole-brain analyses described), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions). Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social attribution task (attributing awareness to a cartoon face) in healthy adult participants (n=50, ages 18–49) and later a TMS follow-up. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (H trials − E trials) with corrected thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinates in Table 1, and figures showing surface maps and time series. Full methods, results, and discussion are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using social tasks (Cyberball exclusion and a modified Dictator Game) probing social processes (punishment and forgiveness), meeting I3. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, mean age 20.7), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with peak coordinates and tables (e.g., Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not truncated), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses include whole-brain results (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity-only or between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (anticipatory active interpersonal touch) in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (multiple Target and Target×Modality contrasts), cluster-corrected statistical maps, conjunctions, and a tactile localizer; results are presented in figures/tables and described for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical report. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of self/other social-cognitive processing (conceptual and agentic self-referential recollection) in healthy adults (N=18; age range 19–29). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation analyses are reported (SPM8 second-level analyses with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables), and results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures description) is present and sufficient for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a competitive (intergroup vs individual) task during fMRI with self-referential/moral stimuli, addressing perception/understanding of self in social context. Sample: healthy adult volunteers (final N=21, Mage=23.1) within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and provides whole-brain results/tables (Table 2) and coordinates; ROI analyses are also used but whole-brain maps are reported. Full article text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates facial color processing, a form of social communication/perception of others (social-related processing). It recruited 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.2), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored faces vs natural-colored scrambled images) used to localize face-selective regions and presents group-level activation maps and coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports original fMRI data during a social feedback task (social-related processing of self/other trait feedback), tested in healthy adult German and Chinese participants. Methods describe whole-brain SPM8 GLM analyses and report group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and corrected clusters (FWE-corrected results, tables and figures) for healthy groups. The sample comprises healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The task probes perception/understanding of self and others (social cognition constructs). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (emotion alignment during dyadic interaction) using an interactive task involving social communication/appraisal. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (students; mean age 23.95), and results are reported for the healthy scanner group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; clusterwise FWE correction) with tables/figures of activations. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study presenting first-person video clips of social interactions (reactive-aggressive, social-positive, neutral) to a sample of 20 healthy adult males (mean age 24.6), satisfying I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and provides peak coordinates/tables (Tables 2–3), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception/understanding (viewing dyadic point-light social interactions while performing an unrelated task), conducted in a healthy adult sample (n=10 males, ages 22–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts [(atypical > typical) including upright/inverted], with cluster-size correction and tables/coordinates of activated regions (i.e., voxelwise whole-brain results are reported). Results are described in text, figures, and tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages within 18–35) that used a social-related task (imagined triadic social interactions, self- and other-referential judgments) during task-based fMRI (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults and results for that group are reported (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (e.g., conjunction analyses, triad > control, with FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult-only sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

Although this fMRI study uses a social task (ultimatum game) in healthy adult participants and reports group-level task-evoked activation, the second-level analyses were performed within a restricted anatomical mask comprising 16 bilateral ROIs rather than as an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore it reports only ROI-masked results and not an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, violating the review's whole-brain requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported unmasked whole-brain voxelwise group-level task map). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (TAP with angry vs. neutral facial expressions) in healthy adult participants. The sample included 32 healthy males (mean age 23.3), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures describing whole-brain results (Tables 1 and 2, whole-brain contrasts and cluster-wise statistics). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social, competitive task (matching-pennies) engaging social cognition/mentalizing (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (analysis on N=16, ages 18–25), satisfying the age/sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (first- and second-level GLM; voxelwise p<.001 with cluster FWE correction) and provides figures and tables of coordinates, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; content appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (impression formation/person evaluation) in healthy adults using a task during scanning (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 19–31 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain ANOVA and Table 1 listing activations), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (meets I5 and I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (ROI analyses are present but not sole; whole-brain results are reported). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (implicit/explicit theory-of-mind false-belief processing) in healthy adults. The sample are healthy adults (mean age 22.7; MRI analyses reported on n=16), satisfying the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and statistical parametric maps with peak coordinates for the explicit ToM localizer (false-belief > false-photo/map) and whole-brain contrasts for the implicit task, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The task is a social-related paradigm (Sally–Anne false-belief movies) and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included in the review.

The available content is limited to abstract, highlights, and metadata (full text incomplete). While the study reports an fMRI neuroimaging component of interpersonal synchrony and social affiliation (satisfying I3), the provided material does not include methods or results needed to confirm sample ages and whether group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for healthy adults are reported. Therefore I4 (sample ages/healthy adult group) and I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on available information, but the inability to confirm key inclusion criteria leads to exclusion pending full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 20–28) that investigates socio-emotional processing (empathy) while participants watched campaign videos. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (CV > NV) with FWE-corrected significance and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures. Behavioral indices of empathic expression are related to BOLD in STS. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (whole-brain contrasts, ROI analyses, tables/figures), and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked map reported; I6: whole-brain results clearly described with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition (voice-face priming), which addresses social perception/understanding of others (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=16, ages 20–31), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (identity and physical-distance contrasts) and provides peak coordinates and statistical results from the healthy group; whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (with ROI-corrected inference reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps or contrasts (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=26, ages 18–39) that used a social-related task (perception of biological motion) and reports both ROI and whole-brain group-level task analyses. The manuscript explicitly describes whole-brain analyses of biological-motion selectivity with correction for multiple comparisons and reports a significant cluster in the right pSTS/TPJ (Fig. S1), satisfying the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (supplemental material referenced but not required). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within the target age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (explicit labeling of others’ emotional facial expressions), with 50 healthy adult participants aged 18–29. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (first- and second-level contrasts and cluster-level FWE-corrected results) and provides tables/coordinates and figures describing group-level activation in the healthy sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–33) that explicitly manipulates a social context (shared vs unshared viewing with a friend) during task-evoked picture viewing. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task activation analyses, including whole-brain results (whole-brain corrected activations reported for DLPFC and precuneus) and ROI results in ventral striatum and OFC; statistical thresholds and cluster corrections are described. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication: participants received text messages believed to be from a friend or a computer and neural responses were measured (social-related processing). Sample: healthy adult participants (N=18 analyzed), ages 19–28, meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (univariate SPM analyses with cluster tables and searchlight MVPA/MVCA results, Figures and Table 2 with MNI coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence; coordinates and maps are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only contrasts, age range appropriate, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of healthy adult participants (scanned n=25, mean age ~22.6) performing a social task (repeated pairwise public good game) that probes social tie formation, affiliation and understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (parametric effects, coordinates, figures, cluster-corrected maps) for the healthy/control group and provides tables and figures with coordinates and thresholding details. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults. The task explicitly probes social communication and mutual understanding. The sample comprises 54 healthy adult participants (27 pairs; ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-level inference, correction for multiple comparisons) and describes whole-brain search results (including localization in rSTG) and statistical procedures; results are reported in main text and supplementary materials. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates joint attention (a social interaction task) in healthy adult participants (final N=13, mean age 24.85), using a virtual-reality, gaze-contingent social task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc), conjunctions, FDR-corrected second-level random-effects maps, and tables/figures with coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met: the task is social-related (I3), the sample consists of healthy adults within the 18–65 range (I4), whole-brain group-level task activation maps are reported (I5), and results are presented in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion: I3 appears satisfied (authors report dyadic fMRI during eye contact, a social-related task). Unable to confirm: I4 (no participant/sample details to verify healthy adults 18–65), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no whole-brain results in text, tables, or figures). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Excluded due to incomplete reporting preventing confirmation of required inclusion criteria; fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults (N=37, ages 20–39) who performed an explicit social-related task (feeling-addressed judgments). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (main effects and interactions) with cluster correction and provides peak coordinates and tables of activations. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and is original empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (person interactions) in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (sex-categorization of dyads manipulating interaction congruency), meeting I3. Participants were healthy adults aged 21–31 (n=12), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses and voxelwise contrasts with cluster correction and tables/figures of whole-brain results (e.g., contrasts incongruent>congruent; Table 3; Figs 6–7), meeting I5 and I6. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (perception of crowd emotion and interaction dynamics), using a task-based design and reporting whole-brain, group-level random-effects ANOVA results with cluster tables and peak coordinates. Sample: 16 healthy adult participants aged 19–27 (within 18–65). Whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/cluster results are reported and described in the text and tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (sender–receiver deception game) investigating socio-cognitive/Theory-of-Mind processes—clearly a social-related task. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age 24.3, range 21–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple contrasts, Bayesian second-level maps) with tables of coordinates and figures. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants predicted others' behavior (desires vs. rules) while undergoing task-based fMRI, addressing Theory-of-Mind and deontic reasoning. Sample: 18 healthy adults aged 18–44 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial second-level models, cluster-level correction and tables of coordinates), and also small-volume corrections; results and coordinates are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references (i.e., core article content present). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group-only; participants are within age range; paper is empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using dyadic (face-to-face) task-based fMRI of eye contact, a clearly social interaction paradigm. Participants: 19 pairs (38 healthy adults, ages 18–33) with demographics reported — meets healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and cluster/coordinate results (GLM group analyses for tasks A/B, paired t-tests, cluster table and atlas labels in MNI space), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (figures/tables and coordinates). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This article appears to be a theoretical/review paper (only abstract and metadata provided) concerning mirror-touch synesthesia; it references fMRI evidence but presents no original fMRI methods, participant sample, or results. Exclusion criterion E6 applies (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task) not met, I4 (healthy adult sample reported) not met, I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map reported) not met, I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results) not met. Full text is incomplete (only abstract/summary available).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI with explicit social attribution conditions (why/how social vs nonsocial task); (I4) Healthy adult sample reported (N=19, ages 21–46); (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (conjunction and interaction whole-brain maps with cluster-level correction) clearly identified for the healthy group; (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. This study is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study using an automatic imitation task manipulated by social-affective cues (affiliation-related constructs: emotional expressions, group membership), meeting the review objective. Sample: 41 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.63), satisfying the age/sampling criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent; masked contrasts for Happy vs Angry, Out-group vs In-group) with cluster-level correction and tables of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are reported for the healthy participant group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, empirical study in healthy adults).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (smiling-face social rewards) in a healthy adult sample (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results including whole-brain (FWE-corrected) activations and ROI and whole-brain tables/figures (e.g., Tables 2–4; whole-brain and small-volume FWE-corrected results are described), clearly from the healthy/control group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study explicitly manipulating social working memory (trait-based ranking of friends) during task performance and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (conjunction and contrasts with cluster/voxel thresholds and tables). Sample: 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 21.56) reported separately. Whole-brain statistical maps/cluster results for the healthy group are presented and used in behavioral correlations. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults investigating social processing (gaze following/observed eye contact), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (contrasts, tables, figures). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6). The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and GLM analyses with group random-effects tests and reported suprathreshold activations (coordinates and tables). Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical fMRI study examines multiple social cognitive tasks (theory of mind, face perception, biological motion, voice perception, language) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses and thresholded activation maps restricted to the STS, with detailed methods, results, and figures describing task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses while participants judged actions at different levels of abstraction using a why/how task. It directly probes social-cognitive constructs (mentalizing/theory-of-mind, understanding actions/intentions) and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain results and ROI-complementary whole-brain maps). The sample consists of healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (N=17 analyzed; ages 21–46). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (including whole-brain and ROI analyses), and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-emotional processing (gender identification of angry/happy faces vs. neutral shapes) in healthy adult participants (N=30, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA; main effects of stimulus type reported with FWE-corrected whole-brain results) and provides coordinates/figures and ROI analyses; whole-brain healthy-group results are clearly attributed to the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI investigation of mentalizing using an interactive social task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a sample of 164 healthy subjects, and describes group-level whole-brain task-associated activations (mentalizing network regions listed in the abstract). These meet inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task results reported), and I6 (results described in text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Note: the provided full text appears to be truncated (abstract, highlights, metadata) rather than the complete article (methods/results/discussion not present), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=37, ages 18–25) that uses a task involving observation and imitation of actions, a social-related process (imitation/social communication and perception of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (parametric modulation, second-level random-effects one-sample t-tests) with tables/figures of results and cluster-corrected thresholds. Whole-brain PPI connectivity is supplementary but task-evoked whole-brain activation maps are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so assessment is possible. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) and measured task-evoked BOLD responses, satisfying I3. The sample consisted of healthy adult undergraduates (ages 18–21), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects results for the social > non-social contrast (FDR-corrected, p<0.05) with accompanying figure and table, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts, and participants fall within the required age range. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., core article content), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social reputation judgments), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=28, ages 20–24), satisfying the sample requirement. The task is social (perception of reputation from faces/words) and uses functional MRI (I3). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (positive vs. neutral, negative vs. neutral, conjunctions) with thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and lists activations in Table 1 and figures (I5,I6). Results are reported for the healthy control group (not limited to a subgroup) (I4). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), it is not a connectivity-only or resting-state study, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the EmpaToM task to probe social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind), i.e., social-related processing. Samples are healthy adult participants (Experiments 1a/1b and 2; age means 26.6–40.9, all within 18–65) with results reported separately for healthy groups. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., emotionally negative vs. neutral videos; ToM vs. nonToM questions), with tables of activation peaks and statistical thresholds and random-effects analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social gaze-following task (political in-group/out-group faces) in healthy adult participants (n=28; ages 18–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (incongruent > congruent), thresholding and cluster results (Table 3, Fig. 2) satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Sample and results pertain to healthy adults and are reported separately. ROI analyses are present but not exclusive; whole-brain effects are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory-of-Mind (social cognition) using the moving-triangles task (meets I3). The sample comprises 20 healthy adults with ages reported as 24–64 (mean 45.6), satisfying the 18–65 healthy-adult requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R; ToM > Baseline) with thresholds, significant clusters, and referenced tables/coordinates (I5). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI investigation of negative emotion processing using IAPS images and focused on sex differences and fronto-limbic connectivity. It does not target social-related processing constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others) but rather general emotional reactivity; although some images contained people and dmPFC/ social-cognition are discussed, the task and aims are emotion-based, not a social cognition task. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–45), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked HA− > NTR contrast), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (task is not a social-related task as defined by the review). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I3.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (empathy for pain modulated by ingroup/outgroup; minimal group paradigm), using a task that targets perception/understanding of others. The sample is healthy adults (n=30, age 18–35) and results for the healthy group are reported separately. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (SPM8 repeated-measures ANOVA; main effect of pain reported at FWE-corrected p≤0.05 with cluster sizes, interaction effects reported with tables/figures), and results are reported in tables of activations (Tables 5-7) and text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical task-based fMRI in healthy adults).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15; mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing dyadic violent interactions with attentional focus on aggressor vs victim), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., focus on aggressor vs victim; whole-brain activation figures and tables), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity or between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI task that manipulates social content (Social vs Non-social passages) and examines Theory of Mind-related processing, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample consists of 26 healthy adult participants (ages 19–26), meeting the adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (Table 1, figures), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are clearly described in text/figures. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, healthy adults in range, empirical fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study combining self-referential and implicit social stimulus processing (social stimuli = pictures depicting humans). Sample: 28 healthy adults aged 30–50 (meets age and healthy-sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (ANOVA across 28 subjects) with FDR-corrected statistical maps, conjunctions, and cluster tables/figures, clearly from the healthy group. Results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion) addressing social-affiliation/attachment processes. Sample consists of healthy adult university students (unmarried young adults) reported separately and analyzed as the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (exclusion vs. inclusion) across all participants with FWE-corrected thresholds and presents whole-brain results in tables and figures (e.g., Tables 3–4, Figures 1–3). Whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables satisfy reporting requirements. Although PPI connectivity analyses are included, whole-brain task activation maps are clearly reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social perception (racial prejudice influencing disgust perception), uses a passive face-viewing social task (perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult sample (N=26, mean age ~21), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and contrasts (interaction and main effects) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures. Although the study also reports PPI connectivity, it additionally presents unmasked whole-brain task activation maps and ROI follow-ups. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (valence classification of agentic vs. communal trait words), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=42, ages 18–25), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, conjunctions, AlphaSim-corrected results) with tables/figures of activations and peak coordinates, meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only). The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (speech-act understanding: Naming vs Requesting) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and provides whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming; Words > Faces) with FDR and SVC corrections, plus tables/figures of activations. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI hyperscanning during social tasks (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~20–23). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (SPM statistics, cluster-level FWE thresholds) with tables of coordinates and figures. Healthy-group results are clearly described separately (e.g., inter-individual synchronization, JA activations). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults (I3, I4) and provides whole-brain group-level task activation results (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a dynamic social gestures (DSG) task that directly probes social versus nonsocial processing (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy young adults (mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7), reported as a healthy adult group and analyzed as such (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FLAME group-level, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with coordinates and tables (Table 1) and figures (meets I5 and I6). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or only out-of-range participants) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of interpersonal trust/distrust (social cognition) using an explicit task to manipulate and measure trustworthiness evaluations pre/post scanning. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=60; mean age ~20.3 years) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., trust+distrust > age; trust > age; distrust > age; direct contrasts) with FWE-corrected thresholds and whole-brain tables/figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps from healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=26; mean age 28.7) using social tasks (face-viewing, person-judgment) that probe perception/understanding of others (satisfies I3). The sample is within the 18–65 range and reported separately for healthy participants (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects parametric analyses (with FWE correction) and tables/figures of voxelwise results (Fig. S1, Table S4), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text and SI, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical).

The full text reports an fMRI experiment using social-emotional (empathy-evoking) film clips with contextual framing and music to probe empathic concern. Sample: 26 healthy adults (age range fits 18–65) with exclusions noted; results for the healthy group are reported separately. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (mixed 2×3 factorial ANOVA, contrasts for sad vs neutral context and multisensory vs unisensory), with tables of significant clusters and FWE-corrected results, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. While the study also includes DCM effective connectivity analyses, it additionally reports univariate whole-brain task maps for the healthy participants. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=29 final, ages 18–27) that used a social-interaction task (perceived live vs. recorded speech) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Live > Social; Social > Standard) thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures/tables describing the maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ mental states) using task-based fMRI and multivariate analyses. Participants are healthy adults (N=20; ages 18–27), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and network-level analyses with voxelwise statistics and cluster correction (t maps, figures, Tables S2/S3), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=26 analyzed; age range 19–37) that uses a task probing social processing (learning about others’ generosity) with a matched non-social control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., Gifter > Lottery, parametric SPE and predictability contrasts) with thresholding and cluster correction, tables of coordinates, figures, and SPM8-based analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) and full methodological details are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata are provided). However, critical details required by the review are missing: participant sample characteristics (healthy adults aged 18–65) are not reported in the provided text (I4 cannot be confirmed), and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates are presented in the abstract/metadata (I5 not met). Because the full article content (methods, detailed results, and group whole-brain maps) is not available here, we cannot verify key inclusion criteria; per screening rules the record must be treated as ineligible until full text is available. The provided content is only an abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). However, the abstract indicates an ROI-based approach (targeting right Superior Temporal Sulcus) and reports correlation analyses between EEG features and that ROI; there is no evidence in the provided content of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from healthy adults. Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) and I5 (whole-brain group-level results) are not met based on the available text. The article reports an fMRI study of social processing (affective theory-of-mind using emotional facial expressions) in healthy adult participants (n=22 recruited, 21 analyzed; mean age 23.7). It provides group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (functional localizer 3rdppA>1stppV; main contrast EFE>no EFE) with voxelwise results, tables of peak coordinates, figures, and cluster-level corrections—clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (effects of empathic vs. unempathic comments) in healthy adults (n=20, mean age 26). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (FWE-corrected clusters, tables, and figures) for the healthy sample, and coordinates/cluster results are presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, participants, fMRI acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral, physiological, whole-brain fMRI contrasts), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI while participants viewed and processed facial expressions (social communication/perception of others) and included an attention task during scanning (I3). The sample consisted of healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 25.2) within the 18–65 range (I4). The authors report group-level mixed-effects analyses and state that parameter-estimate maps for each condition were generated and registered to MNI space, which indicates the presence of group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps (I5). Results are reported in the main text and figures and analyses include whole-brain anatomical-mask comparisons (acceptable reporting formats per I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-evaluative processing using naturalistic videos (social communication/understanding of others). Sample comprises 37 healthy adults (mean age 24.8), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with FWE-corrected results, figures and tables of coordinates, and ROI analyses as complementary work. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social perception (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations), using a social-related task (face perception and trustworthiness ratings) in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (Black>White contrasts, second-level covariate analyses) with peak MNI coordinates, extent/voxel thresholds, and tables/figures describing activations and PPI connectivity. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures meets the reporting criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are not necessary to establish eligibility. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study directly investigates social cognition (linking person perception and person knowledge) using task-based functional MRI. Participants are healthy adults (n=21 analyzed; mean age 24.6) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and tables (e.g., Tables 1 and 2; univariate and PPI analyses described and thresholded), with coordinates and overlap with functional localisers. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating theory-of-mind/social processing using task-based fMRI. Participants: 24 healthy adults (mean age 25.7), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects contrasts (e.g., social > non-social during Background; unexpected > expected in Outcome) with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster results and peak MNI coordinates (Tables 1–3), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (visual social judgment/dominance task) in healthy adults (N=23, ages 21–43). The manuscript provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (Social > Perceptual Judgment) with FWE cluster-corrected maps and a table of peak coordinates (Table 1), clearly reported for the healthy sample. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain healthy-group activation maps.

The study reports an fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (meaning-focused judgments of symbolic artifacts and own-vs-other/collective contrasts) in healthy adult participants (n=25, mean age 24, no neurological/mental history). Analyses used whole-brain, group-level random effects GLM in SPM8 with voxelwise results reported (contrasts such as meaning>physical, own>other, interaction effects) and tables/figures of peak coordinates and corrected statistical thresholds (FDR/FWE). Therefore it meets criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables provided). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (Cyberball) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-corrected results with coordinates. Sample consists of healthy adults (final N=31, mean age ~21) within the 18–65 range. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

Exclusion: E3 (study reports primarily ROI- and seed-based functional connectivity / network analyses without reporting a whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy/control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI probing social-related processing: self-referential / perception-of-self). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task activation map from the healthy/control group is reported); I4 (age eligibility unclear — healthy control ages not reported, so cannot verify 18–65 requirement). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but the reported results are connectivity/network analyses rather than unmasked whole-brain task activation maps required by the review.

This fMRI study examines socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) using a psychotherapist-delivered task (social context) in healthy adult participants (females aged 22–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction, and includes tables/figures of results and coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. "INCLUDED" based on meeting all required inclusion criteria and no exclusions.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) probing retaliation, which is a social-emotional processing construct. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported (thresholds, cluster correction, Talairach coordinates, figures/tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Although the sample is small and male-only (noted as a limitation), this does not violate inclusion requirements for healthy adult whole-brain fMRI task activation reporting.

The available content (highlights, abstract, and references) indicates an fMRI social (mentalizing/prisoner’s dilemma) study in healthy adults and reports neural activation findings; therefore I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) appear satisfied. However the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/highlights/references), so I cannot verify that the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5). I cannot confirm whether whole-brain results are presented (tables/figures/supplement) as required by I5/I6. Because I5 is not verifiable from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this stage. Full text incomplete; recommend obtaining the complete article to reassess.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking, attention shifts) in healthy adult participants (n=33, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (searchlight MVPA and GLMs) with voxelwise FWE-corrected results and tables of significant clusters/coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (social-related fMRI tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps and contrasts reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text and tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) using the EmpaToM paradigm in a healthy adult sample (N=178, mean age 40.9). The sample is within the 18–65 age range and results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (modified Cyberball) that manipulates social exclusion and public performance evaluation, addressing social processing. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference vs other-reference) in healthy adults (N=110, age 19–31).
