This fMRI study investigates social evaluations (intelligence/friendliness) from faces in healthy adults and reports task-evoked voxelwise results, but all voxelwise statistical tests were restricted to an a priori set of ROIs (search regions restricted to amygdala, insula, IFG, ACC, thalamus, caudate, mOFC). No unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain reporting requirement.

The article reports task fMRI including a social cognition (theory-of-mind/social interaction vs random movement) task (meets I3). Samples are healthy adult participants from HCP (ages 22–36) and UCLA dataset (ages 21–50), clearly within 18–65 (meets I4). The Methods and Results describe voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and display task activation maps (e.g., Figure 1) derived from healthy/control groups, satisfying the whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map requirement (meets I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/seed-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=55, mean age 24.9) using a social-related task (erotic and fearful social scenes and faces) with intranasal oxytocin manipulation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and results (multiple contrasts) with whole-brain FWE-corrected statistics (e.g., erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mind perception and gaze-cueing) in healthy adults (N=22; mean age 24.36). The study collected task-based functional MRI during a mind-perception task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1, cluster-corrected results; see reported tables and figures). Whole-brain results are described in the text and tables (e.g., Table 4) and conjunction analyses are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using an emotional face recognition task (social perception/understanding of others) in adult mothers, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (CON; mothers without early life maltreatment or lifetime mental disorder) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for the control group (e.g., familiarity effect own>unknown in CON: medial frontal gyrus, whole-brain pFWE<0.001), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain map. Whole-brain and ROI analyses are both reported; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not a between-groups-only report, and participants are adults within 18–65). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-related relationship episodes) in healthy adults (final N=35, screened for mental disorders). The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with cluster-level inference and FDR correction, and includes tables/figures of activation peaks. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review: I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text unavailable (publisher page returns 404). Only metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) available. Cannot verify required inclusion criteria: I3 (task-based fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation map for healthy/control group), and I6 (results clearly reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available information. Because core article content (methods, results) is missing, the study cannot be reliably assessed and must be excluded pending retrieval of the complete full text. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion IDs met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), meeting I3. The sample comprises 24 healthy adult participants (mean age 26), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected), with figures and coordinates described in the text, meeting I5 and I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback) meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy younger adult group (ages 20–33) satisfying the sample age requirement and reports group-level voxelwise analyses: a whole-brain ANOVA (age × feedback × trait), cluster-level results, and a whole-brain replication reported (see Supplementary Table 2 and figures). Results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, non-eligible age-only samples, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mental state attribution/prediction), using a task that elicits judgments about others' mental states (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 18–22; N=28 after exclusion), satisfying the adult healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and corrected statistical maps (searchlight RSA and repetition-suppression results with MNI coordinates and TFCE-corrected p-values), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Reporting of whole-brain results in figures and text meets the allowance for coordinates/figures/supplement (I6). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (N=20 males, ages 21–37). The task is clearly social in nature (cooperation/trust feedback and ratings), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial analyses, cluster-level FWE-corrected results) with reported activation clusters and tables/figures, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Healthy adult results are reported separately (within-subject, placebo vs MDMA). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) collected during BOLD fMRI, satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22, meeting I4. The authors report group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM, whole-brain thresholding, cluster inference) and present whole-brain results and clusters for the healthy groups (including analyses for all genotypes and rs53576 GG subgroup), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered: the paper includes whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses, is not limited to connectivity/resting-state-only analyses, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects, and the participants fall within the 18–65 range. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 – task is social-related (provocation, social decision-making); I4 – sample comprises healthy adult males aged 18–35; I5 – whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts are reported (high>low provocation during feedback and decision phases) with SPM12 and cluster-level FWE correction; I6 – whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not limited to between-group contrasts without a healthy-group task map, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy adults (N=44, mean age 22.4). The paradigm is a social interactive game probing perception/understanding of others and social exchange. Group-level whole-brain task analyses are reported (GLM, FLAME, non-parametric 'randomize' correction) with tables of clusters and thresholded maps described in the text and figures. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only DOI/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI social-reward (pleasant touch) task and a healthy control group, so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 appear satisfied. However I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because the full text (methods/results/figures/tables) is not available to verify whole-brain healthy-group task effects, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are identifiable from the abstract. Therefore I exclude this record pending access to the complete full text so that I5 can be verified.

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/header and title present). Cannot verify whether the study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task in healthy adults, or whether it provides whole-brain, healthy-group task-evoked maps. Title indicates a sample of young adult males with autism and mentions resting state and overt social interaction, but methods and results are not available in the provided content. Therefore inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the available information.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights provided). From the abstract, the study uses task-based fMRI to assess theory of mind (I3 met). However, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified: sample age ranges for healthy adult group (I4) are not specified in the provided content, and the presence of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group statistical map (I5) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on available information. Full text required to confirm whole-brain task activation reporting and participant ages; absent that, I exclude due to inability to verify all inclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata/highlights present). The study addresses social-related processing (dynamic facial expression processing in pSTS) so I3 is met. However participant details and ages are not reported in the provided content, so I4 cannot be confirmed. The provided content does not report or show group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy group, so I5 cannot be confirmed; I6 likewise cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available text. Because the core article content (methods, participants, and full results/figures) is missing, I exclude this record pending full text access.

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception of others) in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: N=20, mean age ~25). The study reports group-level fMRI analyses (mixed-effects FLAME) and uses an independent group-level localizer (n=83) to derive face-selective ROIs from a faces>scrambled contrast, indicating availability of group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and links neural results to behavioral tasks. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task analyses/contrast), and I6 (acceptable reporting format) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of live social interaction (bidirectional conversation) contrasting human–human vs human–robot interactions, directly addressing social communication/mentalizing and social motivation (I3). Sample includes 21 healthy adults (mean age 25.8), meeting the adult 18–65 criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (e.g., HHI vs HRI) with cluster-level FDR correction and renders results (figures and NeuroVault link), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study probing social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure toward human vs. robot) using task-based fMRI and a socializing intervention. The sample is healthy adults (n=26, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected results) and provides whole-brain contrast maps (NeuroVault/OSF). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (co-speech gestures during naturalistic narrative) in healthy adults. Sample: 20 right-handed native German speakers, ages 22–35 (meets adult 18–65 criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID; speech > gestures+speech; gestures+speech > speech), thresholding, cluster extents, coordinates and tables/figures (satisfies whole-brain reporting and acceptable formats). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables — not truncated. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; healthy-group task effects are directly reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

This fMRI study uses a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD vs HC, NSSI vs HC, conjunctions) and does not present an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map for the healthy control group (no clear healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map). I6 is also not met because there are no clearly described whole-brain healthy-group results in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete. Excluding on E4 to maintain requirement for explicit healthy-group whole-brain activation maps needed for meta-analysis of healthy adult task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=111, ages 19–36; fMRI analyses report data from N=36/38 grouped participants) that investigates perception of animacy — a perceptual precursor to social cognition and falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., conjunction contrasts, whole-brain FWE-corrected maps, searchlight MVPA) and provides coordinates and figures of whole-brain effects. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based fMRI data using multiple clearly social-related tasks (false belief/ToM, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, vocalizations, face tasks) satisfying the review's scope. The sample consists of 78 healthy adult participants (ages 18–40, N=78 in fMRI), satisfying the sample criterion. The authors present group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM RFX) with FWE-corrected thresholds and list peak coordinates and maps (figures, supplementary tables, NeuroVault links), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (observation of dynamic facial expressions) in healthy adults (n=51, mean age 22.5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (dynamic facial expressions vs dynamic mosaics) analyzed at the group level with family-wise error correction and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets I3 (task fMRI of vocal emotional/social communication processing) and I4 (healthy adult sample, N=36, ages 20–35). However, it does NOT report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinate-based whole-brain activation results. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based (Power-264) FC and graph-theoretical network metrics rather than voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps; therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This triggers exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). I6 is not applicable because no whole-brain results are provided in tables/figures. Exclusion based on E2.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (trust, advice-taking) in healthy adults (N=31, mean age 24.3). The paper reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked results (univariate GLMs with voxel/FWE-corrected maps, MVPA whole-brain searchlight, tables of coordinates and figures) clearly for the healthy/control group. The methods, results, and figures describing whole-brain analyses and coordinates are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Neuroimage acquisition/preprocessing details).

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates neural responses to vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds, addressing social-related auditory processing (social communication/perception). It includes healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (vocal > non-vocal; voxelwise thresholding, FDR-corrected, cluster thresholds, and MNI coordinates are provided and discussed), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used task-based fMRI while participants (including a healthy neurotypical adult control group) observed socio-affective touch videos. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy/control group (univariate contrasts with pFWE thresholds and supplementary tables/figures with peak coordinates and maps), and includes multivariate analyses. The healthy control group (N=21) is explicitly reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining how collective/social schemas (collective memory, social knowledge) shape individual memory representations. The task involves recall of museum pictures with analyses focused on medial PFC regions implicated in social cognition (dmPFC/vmPFC), addressing social-related processing. Sample: 24 healthy adults aged 22–39, meeting the healthy adult criterion. Whole-brain group-level searchlight analyses (TFCE-corrected) are reported, providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.
